task.title: Build a 4-player online Texas Hold'em poker game
request: Add a new game to this Browser Games monorepo: an online multiplayer Texas
Hold'em poker game that FOUR people can play together over the network, each
from their own browser. Follow the repo's existing conventions (Vite + React
workspace; new code under games/ and/or packages/ as appropriate) rather than
dropping in a standalone static app.
Architecture (multiplayer is the core requirement):
- An authoritative Node WebSocket server that owns the game state: shuffles and
deals, runs the betting rounds (pre-flop, flop, turn, river, showdown),
enforces turn order and legal actions, manages the pot and dealer button, and
determines the winner by standard hand ranking. Clients NEVER see other
players' hole cards.
- A browser client that connects over WebSocket, lets a player join a table by
name, shows their two hole cards + the shared community cards + the pot + whose
turn it is, and offers the legal actions (fold / check / call / bet-raise) for
the player on action. Four separate browser sessions = four players at one
table.
Correct Texas Hold'em rules: blinds, betting rounds, side pots are out of scope
for v1 (a single main pot is fine), but turn order, legal-action enforcement,
the five-card-best-hand evaluation at showdown, and awarding the pot to the
winner MUST be correct. Put the hand-evaluation and game-engine logic in a
pure, unit-testable module and cover it with unit tests (vitest).
Use accessible, user-facing markup (buttons/labels with real text) so a
Playwright test can drive players with getByRole.
In the QA/validation stage: (1) run the engine unit tests, and (2) write and run
a Playwright end-to-end test that boots the server and FOUR browser clients,
seats them at one table, plays a full hand through to showdown with each client
taking a legal action when it is their turn, and asserts that exactly one winner
is announced and awarded the pot. Record it with video + trace ON and leave the
recording as proof.
